step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture was derived by first identifying all visual components on the whiteboard diagram. This included icons for SFTP, S3, Lambda, Rekognition, and two user/actor icons (one with a camera, one general user). The text labels associated with these icons were used to determine the AWS service where applicable. The transcript was then used to confirm service names and provide additional context, such as 'Amazon Transfer Family' for SFTP and the two distinct processing layers ('INSTANT' and 'BATCH'). Grouped dashed boxes were treated as logical groupings, with individual services within them represented as separate nodes as per the visual cues. Edges were drawn strictly based on the arrows present on the whiteboard, following the flow of data from the camera, through processing, to the end-user. Flow IDs and sequence numbers were assigned to represent the logical progression of data through the system, starting with image ingestion, followed by instant and batch processing, and finally user access.

graph.name: B2B Multi-tenant Construction Site Monitoring and Progress Solution
graph.categories: Image Processing, Serverless, AI/ML, Data Ingestion, Storage
graph.notes: This architecture describes a B2B multi-tenant solution for construction site monitoring that processes and obfuscates images using serverless components and Amazon Rekognition, including custom labels for enhanced detection. It handles about 86,000 images daily.

nodes.name: Construction Site Camera
nodes.notes: Cameras worldwide ingesting approximately 86,000 images per day.

nodes.name: SFTP
nodes.notes: Amazon Transfer Family (SFTP) used by each tenant to connect their camera easily.

nodes.name: Input S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: First injection layer where raw images are stored before processing.

nodes.name: Instant Processor Lambda
nodes.notes: AWS Lambda function for immediate processing of newly uploaded images in the 'INSTANT' layer.

nodes.name: Instant Rekognition
nodes.notes: Amazon Rekognition used in the 'INSTANT' layer to find coordinates for blurring persons and license plates.

nodes.name: Processed Images S3 Bucket
nodes.notes: Bucket storing processed (blurred) images, serving as the platform for customers.

nodes.name: Batch Processor Lambda
nodes.notes: AWS Lambda function for batch processing, running overnight, in the 'BATCH' layer.

nodes.name: Rekognition Custom Labels
nodes.notes: Amazon Rekognition with custom labels, trained on construction workers, used in the 'BATCH' layer to improve accuracy.

nodes.name: Customer Web Platform User
nodes.notes: Customers access processed images and project progress via an S3-backed website.

edges.notes: Image ingestion from cameras to SFTP endpoint.
Images are uploaded to the initial S3 bucket for storage.
New image uploads to S3 trigger the instant processing Lambda function.
Lambda invokes Amazon Rekognition for instant image analysis (blurring persons/license plates).
Processed images from instant analysis are stored in the output S3 bucket.
Images in the input S3 bucket are processed by the batch Lambda (e.g., on a schedule).
Batch Lambda invokes Amazon Rekognition with custom labels for specific object detection (e.g., construction workers).
Results from batch processing (improved accuracy findings) are stored in the output S3 bucket.
Users access the processed and archived images via a platform hosted from the S3 website bucket.
